attributes.magic: PE32+ executable (native) x86-64, for MS Windows

crowdsourced_ai_results.analysis: The sample is a 64-bit Windows kernel driver that implements the NDIS User-mode I/O (NDISUIO) and WWAN (Wireless Wide Area Network) protocols. It creates device objects like `\Device\Ndisuio` and `\Device\WwanProt` to facilitate communication between user-mode applications and network adapter miniports. The driver's functions, imports, and strings (e.g., "NDIS User mode I/O driver", ETW provider "Microsoft-Windows-WWAN-NDISUIO-EVENTS") are all consistent with the legitimate Microsoft `ndisuio.sys` driver. No malicious behaviors were observed.
